text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the "silent killer" because it typically causes no symptoms at all. You can have high blood pressure for years without feeling any changes, which is why regular screening is critical.
snippet_highlighted_words: typically causes no symptoms at all

text_blocks.snippet: In most cases, warning signs only appear if your blood pressure spikes to dangerously high levels (known as a hypertensive crisis, generally above 180/120 mm Hg) or if organ damage has developed over time.
Potential signs of severely elevated blood pressure include:

list.snippet: Headaches (especially severe or throbbing headaches that come on suddenly)
Blurty vision or other vision changes

text_blocks.snippet: When to Seek Emergency Help (Hypertensive Crisis)
If your blood pressure reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher, wait one minute and test it again.

list.snippet: If the second reading is still 180/120 mm Hg or higher and you have any of the following warning signs, call 911 immediately:
If your reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher but you do not have any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider right away for guidance.

text_blocks.snippet: Review official guidance on blood pressure numbers and risks from the American Heart Association or learn more via the Mayo Clinic High Blood Pressure Guide.
